newsitem.title: FINLAND: SINEBRYCHOFF SEES FLAT '97 BEER SALES, PRICE HIKES.
newsitem.headline: SINEBRYCHOFF SEES FLAT '97 BEER SALES, PRICE HIKES.

text.p: Finnish brewer Oy Sinebrychoff Ab said in a statement on Wednesday it did not expect domestic beer sales to increase this year and warned of pressures to hike prices already in spring as costs were on the rise.
"It is well-founded to assume that domestic beer sales will not increase this year," Sinebrychoff managing director Kaj Forssell said in the statement.

Sales volumes had not recovered despite the introduction of new packages. "But costs have risen. Because of that I predict that if domestic beer sales don't rise and the state doesn't lower the (beer) tax, pressures to hike beer prices will emerge before summer," he said.
In 1996, Finnish beer sales fell 1.9 percent. Sinebrychoff said its own market share in beer sales rose to 36.2 percent from 35.9 percent.
But in soft drinks and mineral waters, where domestic sales volumes rose clearly, Sinebrychoff said it had lost ground.
It said group 1996 earnings were at the level of 1995 despite a fall in net sales but gave no details.
